summary: Full backend + frontend verification of Stone 1 — QRU Decoder Engine™ v2.0 at /decoder-engine. All 11 requested acceptance criteria PASS. Backend: 9/9 pytest tests pass in 138s at /app/backend/tests/test_decoder_engine_stone1.py (JUnit at /app/test_reports/pytest/decoder_engine_stone1.xml). Frontend: Founder login → /decoder-engine → decoder-kr-select populated with 40 verified KRs → shelf-filter 'Founder Review Required' shows 3 items (incl. fresh DEC-00005 created during backend tests) → detail view renders 18 scorecard rows (6 deterministic + 12 AI-advisory), all 5 understanding-checks (explain/recognize/apply/correct/teach), analogy_mapping renders as object safely (regression fix holds), safety banner + Medical/Financial/Safety flag chip shown. Action gating verified: Certify Treasure Standard™ is DISABLED at 'Founder Review Required', becomes ENABLED only after Approve moves state to 'Founder Approved'; Approve then disables (canApprove=false). End-to-end lifecycle click-path Approve→Certify succeeded in UI on DEC-00005 (state: Founder Review Required → Founder Approved → Treasure Standard Certified), toast 'Treasure Standard™ certified.' fired, review-history section shows 3 audit entries and the detail view stays in-factory (no forced navigation/download). Export button is present but optional. Backend covers: taxonomy has exactly 15 states (incl. Verification/Educational/Accessibility/Brand Review), verified-krs endpoint returns Knowledge-First list, decode returns 38-field contract with source_kr_ids preserving kr_code+version, 5-part understanding checks, scorecard.deterministic_ok flag + 18 rows, review_state='Founder Review Required', treasure_standard_certified=false, first decode is_canonical=true. Append-only versioning verified: re-decoding the same KR yielded decoder_version>=2 with is_canonical=false while the v1 canonical stayed retrievable. Permission gates verified: certify-before-approve returns HTTP 400 with 'Founder Approved' in the message; approve then certify returns 200 with treasure_standard_certified=true and review_history includes both 'Founder Approved' and 'Treasure Standard Certified'. Request-revision → Archive path validated on a separate fresh decode. Knowledge-First rejection validated: attempting to decode an unverified KR from /api/knowledge/records returned HTTP 400.
critical_code_review_comments: decoder_engine.py:163 — versioning counts by source_kr_ids.kr_id only. If two decodes for the SAME KR run concurrently, both may see count=0 and each create an is_canonical=true record (race condition). Consider a unique-index guard on {kr_id, is_canonical:true} or an atomic findAndUpdate/insert transaction. Very unlikely at Founder-only manual cadence, but worth documenting.

decoder_engine.py:164 — decoder_id is generated by `count_documents({}) + 1`. If any decoder is later hard-deleted, ID reuse is possible and could collide with an audit-log DEC-xxxxx. Use an append-only monotonic counter in a `_seq` collection to prevent reuse.

decoder_engine.py:79 — deterministic_checks() uses `kr_ids_of(kr)` (returns [kr.get('id')]) so the `overpromise` guard's condition `len(kr_ids_of(kr)) <= 1` is ALWAYS true; the guard effectively always applies to any title with overpromise keywords. If the intent was 'overpromise is only a problem when sourced from a SINGLE KR', that reads correctly today but multi-source support isn't wired in yet — flag as a known limitation.

decoder_engine.py:_transition() rebuilds `review_history` client-side and $set's the whole array — not atomic. Two rapid Founder actions could clobber each other. Consider `$push` instead of `$set` on `review_history`.

routers/decoder_engine.py:47 — the decode POST holds the FastAPI request-thread open for 30-90s while calling two LLMs (GEN + advisory). Under any load this will exhaust the ASGI worker pool. Consider making it a background task returning a decoder_id immediately, then polling /shelf. Non-blocking for Founder-only use but architecturally worth noting.

routers/decoder_engine.py — GET /{did} does not disambiguate `id` vs `decoder_id`. Since DecoderEngine.js uses `selected.id` (Mongo id) this works, but any operator hitting the API with DEC-00005 will get 404. Consider accepting either field.

DecoderEngine.js:118 — exportJson uses `a.click()` on a synthesized anchor; on iOS Safari this doesn't trigger a download (returns silently). If Export is intended to work everywhere, provide a data-URL fallback or open the JSON in a new tab.

DecoderEngine.js:79 — .catch(() => {}) silently swallows shelf/stats errors; if the API 500s the Founder sees an empty shelf and empty stats with no indication. A small error chip would be honest to Treasure Standard™.

DecoderEngine.js:236 — window.prompt() for revision notes is functional but not accessible / not brand-consistent with the rest of the QRU UI (which uses styled dialogs). Consider a shadcn Dialog for the revision note.

DecoderEngine.js:113 — Field renders unknown objects as JSON.stringify(v). For nested arrays inside objects (e.g., analogy_mapping with array values) the output can look messy. Consider a small recursive renderer or a specialized card for common shapes (analogy_mapping, visual_spec).

DecoderEngine.js:396 — the Provenance & Metadata section (containing decoder_id, kr_code, version, decoded_by, shelf_location) is inside a collapsible Section that defaults to CLOSED. The spec says 'secondary collapsible sections for provenance/metadata/rationale/scorecard' — scorecard IS primary/expanded, and provenance IS collapsible, so this matches spec. Just calling out that Founder must click to see the audit surface.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Stone 1 (Decoder Engine v2.0) is production-ready. Decode uses REAL LLM (Emergent key) — allow up to 180s per decode call; keep DECODE_TIMEOUT=180 in tests. IDs increment across the whole `decoder_records` collection (DEC-#####), so if you decode again the next id will be DEC-00006+. Backend tests are structured with class-scoped fixtures per lifecycle path (approve/certify uses one fresh decode; revise/archive uses another) to avoid interference. `treasure_standard_certified: true` is only set via /certify-treasure endpoint after state==Founder Approved — do not try to shortcut this. The Knowledge-First gate test uses /api/knowledge/records to find an unverified KR — if none exist it skips. Frontend: session uses localStorage key `qru_token`, api client is at `/lib/api` with baseURL from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL + '/api'.
